proposer.mechanism: Adaptive-Threshold AFG: identical mechanics to base AFG (single 10s rolling window, signed aggressor flow, skip open orders when net_flow is adverse), EXCEPT the flow_threshold is no longer a fixed constant. Instead, at each order, compute total_volume = sum of |signed_vol| over the same 10s window (the unsigned activity); set effective_threshold = max(base_threshold, imbalance_ratio * total_volume). With base_threshold=2.0 (the same noise floor as AFG) and imbalance_ratio=0.20 (default), the gate fires on a BUY order when net_flow <= -effective_threshold. In thin periods (total_volume < 10), the fixed 2.0 floor applies (identical to AFG). In busy periods (total_volume = 50), the gate requires net_flow <= -10 â€” i.e., a genuine 20% imbalance â€” rather than firing on a trivial 2-contract residual. Reduce-only orders always submit; after any skip, _position_flat=True so the next open is unconditional (identical anti-cascade to base AFG).
proposer.inefficiency_exploited: Base AFG's fixed flow_threshold=2.0 is dimensionally wrong: it treats a 2-contract net-adverse residual as equally informative regardless of whether the underlying activity in the window was 5 contracts or 100. In active periods, a 2-contract residual is statistical noise (a single late print can flip the sign), not adverse pressure. Base AFG therefore generates many false-positive skips in active periods â€” skipping trades where there is no genuine imbalance, only sampling noise. Conversely, in thin periods, AFG's threshold is appropriately conservative. The adaptive scaling preserves AFG's selectivity in thin markets while suppressing noise-driven false skips in active markets. Prior pc-experiment evidence (r1 burst-only gate: $487 vs base AFG $1255) confirms that gating on a SHARPER feature than the existing AFG level signal can underperform AFG; the right direction is to refine AFG's existing skip criterion, not replace it with an orthogonal one.
proposer.why_survives_costs: Zero commission and zero slippage cost model (verified from execution_algos/aggressor-flow-gate/results/backtest-results.json: mean_slippage=0.0, total_commissions=0.0). Edge accrues entirely as realized_pnl. Base AFG: realized_pnl=$1255.50 over 12-day train window, 107,198 trades, +704.8% vs simple baseline. The adaptive-threshold variant is expected to make MORE precise skip decisions: fewer noise-driven false-positive skips in busy periods (the bulk of AFG's volume â€” the busiest 4 days have ~20k trades each, where AFG's fixed 2-contract threshold is most noise-sensitive), while preserving AFG's correct skips on genuinely imbalanced periods. Pre-committed falsifiable prediction: realized_pnl on the 12-day train window will exceed base AFG's $1255.50 by at least 5% (PASS margin); if the adaptive threshold instead just reduces overall skip rate without improving per-skip precision, realized_pnl will be flat or worse than base AFG and the hypothesis is falsified.
proposer.builds_on: aggressor-flow-gate (base) â€” preserves the signed-flow primitive, single-window structure, reduce-only/anti-cascade semantics, and trade-tick subscription pattern. Replaces only the constant flow_threshold with a max(constant, ratio*total_unsigned_volume) expression. ALSO informed by afg-pc-r1 negative result: a pure orthogonal replacement (burst gate) underperforms AFG by ~$767, so this proposal refines rather than replaces AFG's core skip criterion.
proposer.alternatives_considered: (a) Hybrid AFG-AND-burst gate (level skip only when also accelerating) â€” rejected: r1's per-day table shows AFG-style level skips drive the heavy-loss-day edge (12, 13, 16); ANDing with burst would weaken precisely those wins. (b) Probabilistic/proportional skip (skip with probability scaling with |net_flow|) â€” rejected: introduces RNG, complicates determinism, and the binary decision is fine if the threshold is right. (c) Replace _position_flat anti-cascade with conditional re-entry (only re-enter when flow reverses) â€” rejected as it changes too much at once; if adaptive threshold succeeds, this is a clean follow-up. (d) Per-side asymmetric thresholds â€” rejected: oracle is symmetric (sigma=6.0, seed=42), no directional asymmetry expected. (e) Window-length tuning (3s/15s suggested in r1 NOTES) â€” rejected: r1's per-day numbers don't strongly suggest window length is the binding constraint; the residual loss days (10, 11) are small and the win days are large, so reshape selectivity (threshold), not window. (f) EWMA-based effective threshold rather than discrete max(floor, ratio*vol) â€” rejected: introduces hyperparameter (decay constant) without clear benefit over the explicit floor+ratio form.

objections.text: The proposer mis-identifies the source of base AFG's edge. Base AFG already skips at ~21.6% rate (107,198 of 136,734 baseline trades â€” verified from results/backtest-results.json trade_count=107198 vs simple's 136,734). It produces realized_pnl=$1255.50 (+704.8% vs simple). The 'false-positive skip' framing assumes AFG over-skips, but the empirical evidence is the opposite: AFG is already filtering aggressively and is highly profitable. The proposed adaptive threshold STRICTLY relaxes the gate (effective_threshold >= base_threshold always, with equality only when total_volume <= base_threshold/imbalance_ratio = 10). So in any active period â€” i.e., the bulk of the train window where AFG generates most edge â€” the new gate fires LESS often than AFG. This means LESS of AFG's skip set, not better-quality skips. The hypothesis that AFG's skips in active periods are 'noise-driven' is unsupported â€” they may well be precisely the skips that drive AFG's +$1255 P&L.

Look at the per-day evidence in afg-pc-r1's NOTES. r1's burst-only gate underperformed base AFG ($487 vs $1255) by $768 because it skipped FEWER trades than AFG (6.83% vs AFG's 21.6%) and missed AFG's level-driven skips. r1 ONLY beat AFG on the heaviest-flow days. The proposed adaptive-threshold gate has the same structural problem: by raising the effective threshold in active periods, it will skip fewer adverse-flow moments than AFG. The proposer's own framing â€” 'r1 underperformed because it gated on a sharper signal that missed AFG's level skips' â€” applies equally to this proposal, which makes AFG's level threshold harder to clear.

Unconsidered superior alternative: tighten or LOWER the AFG threshold rather than raise it. If AFG's skips are already +704% precision-positive, then the residual edge to capture is in MORE skips at lower flow magnitudes, not fewer. A simple direction: lower flow_threshold from 2.0 to 1.0 (or 0.5), which would gate on smaller residuals â€” more aggressive skipping. Conversely, the OPPOSITE-direction refinement also untried: differentiate the COOL-DOWN. Base AFG resets _position_flat=True after one skip, throwing away gate info on the very next signal. A natural refinement: keep gating active for K signals post-skip (no unconditional re-entry) â€” captures persistent adverse-flow regimes that AFG currently bleeds through after the first skip. Neither direction was considered in this proposal.

The imbalance_ratio=0.20 default is unmotivated â€” picked by intuition. With base_threshold=2.0 the crossover is at total_volume=10 (10*0.2=2.0). Below that, identical to AFG; above, more permissive. Why 20% and not 10% or 50%? No empirical anchor; depends entirely on the (untested) noise structure of net_flow vs total_volume in MES at 10s scale.

Subtle dimensional issue: total_volume in the 10s window is the sum of |signed_vol|, which approximates total trade size. But in busy periods, two-sided activity (50 BUYS, 50 SELLS, net 0) would yield total_volume=100 and require net_flow<=-20 to skip â€” a 20% net imbalance. That's a reasonable gating criterion if such moments are rare; but in moderately busy periods (10 BUYS + 10 SELLS, net 0, total=20) it requires net_flow<=-4 â€” exactly DOUBLE AFG's threshold. There's no evidence this is the right scaling â€” it may simply gate out moderate-conviction skips that AFG was catching correctly.

suggested_alternatives: Lower base AFG's flow_threshold from 2.0 to ~1.0 â€” explicit edge-extension in the direction AFG's empirical strength already points (skip MORE marginal-imbalance moments).

Sticky cool-down: after a skip, suppress _position_flat reset for K subsequent signals (e.g., K=2 or 3) â€” captures persistent-adverse-flow regimes that AFG currently bleeds through immediately after the first skip.

Volume-relative gate as a SECONDARY tightener (intersected with AFG's gate), not as a relaxer: skip when AFG's level gate fires AND |net_flow|/total_volume exceeds some imbalance ratio â€” strictly more selective skips.
criticizer.reasoning: The proposed adaptive threshold STRICTLY relaxes AFG's gate in active periods (where AFG generates most of its $1255 edge), and the empirical evidence from r1 explicitly shows that gates which skip LESS than AFG underperform AFG by hundreds of dollars. The proposal also fails to consider the cleaner directional refinements (tighten threshold, sticky cool-down) that align with AFG's empirical strength rather than against it.

proposer.mechanism: Persistent-Flow AFG: identical to base AFG (single 10s rolling window of signed aggressor flow; skip BUY when net_flow<=-2.0, skip SELL when net_flow>=+2.0; reduce-only always submits), EXCEPT the post-skip anti-cascade is replaced with a CONDITIONAL re-entry that preserves gating during persistent adverse-flow regimes. Specifically: maintain a counter consecutive_skips. After a skip, do NOT set _position_flat=True. On the next open order: (a) if the gate evaluates as NOT adverse (net_flow has cleared or reversed), submit normally, reset consecutive_skips=0; (b) if the gate evaluates as adverse, increment consecutive_skips â€” if consecutive_skips >= max_consecutive_skips (default 3), force-submit unconditionally and reset (hard cap to break cascades); else skip again. This preserves AFG's exact skip criterion but extends gating across up to 3 successive adverse-flow signals before the hard cap fires. The reduce-only and warm-up (empty deque) paths are unchanged. Trade-tick subscription identical to base AFG. No look-ahead: deque pruned by ts_event <= order.ts_init at decision time.
proposer.inefficiency_exploited: Base AFG's hard _position_flat=True reset after every skip is a documented anti-cascade safeguard, but for AFG specifically it is over-conservative: persistent adverse-flow regimes (sellers continuing to dump for several seconds) are precisely the situations where multiple consecutive entries are likely to face adverse selection. With oracle signal_interval_seconds=1.0, AFG's reset means the very next 1s after a skip submits unconditionally â€” re-entering directly into the still-adverse regime. The criticizer's round 1 observation that 'AFG's skips are precision-positive and drive +$1255 P&L' implies the converse: the entries AFG currently forces through immediately after a skip are precision-NEGATIVE â€” they are the same regime AFG just correctly identified as adverse. Persistent-Flow AFG extends gating across the regime: up to 3 successive adverse signals are skipped (a 3s persistent regime), and a hard cap prevents pathological lock-out. Unlike round 1's adaptive-threshold proposal, this STRICTLY ADDS to AFG's skips (more skip moments, all derived from AFG's already-validated level criterion) rather than relaxing them.
proposer.why_survives_costs: Zero commission, zero slippage cost model (verified). Edge accrues entirely as realized_pnl. Base AFG: realized_pnl=$1255.50, +704.8% vs simple, skip rate 21.6%. Persistent-Flow AFG is expected to skip MORE than AFG (each post-skip gated signal that fires adds 1 to the skip count vs AFG's 0), with the additional skips being structurally similar to AFG's primary skips (same level criterion). If persistent adverse-flow regimes typically span 1-3 seconds (consistent with MES microstructure literature on aggressor-flow autocorrelation), the additional skips will be highly correlated with the original adverse regime and therefore precision-positive. Pre-committed falsifiable prediction: realized_pnl on the 12-day train window will exceed base AFG's $1255.50 by at least 5% (PASS margin); if persistent regimes are NOT the dominant adverse-selection structure (i.e., AFG's single-skip-then-reset is already optimal), realized_pnl will be flat or worse than base AFG and the hypothesis is falsified.
proposer.builds_on: aggressor-flow-gate (base) â€” preserves the signed-flow primitive, 10s window, 2.0 threshold, level-based skip criterion, reduce-only short-circuit, trade-tick subscription, and look-ahead-free pruning. Replaces only the post-skip _position_flat=True reset with a counter-based conditional re-entry capped at max_consecutive_skips=3. ALSO informed by afg-pc-r1 negative result: r1's burst-only gate failed because it skipped LESS than AFG; this proposal addresses the opposite â€” extending AFG's skip set on a principled axis (persistence across the signal stream).
proposer.alternatives_considered: (a) Adaptive threshold (round 1 of this run, REJECTED by criticizer): mechanically relaxes the gate in active periods where AFG drives most of its edge. (b) Lower flow_threshold from 2.0 to 1.0 (criticizer suggestion): viable but unprincipled â€” it just multiplies skip count without changing which TYPES of regimes are caught. The persistent-flow proposal is more selective: it adds skips only when persistence indicates a regime, not blanket lowering. (c) Sticky cool-down for K signals unconditionally post-skip (a simpler version of this proposal): rejected as too crude â€” it would skip the next K signals regardless of whether flow has actually cleared, including in cases where the adverse wave has reversed (which would force the algo to miss favorable opportunities). The conditional re-entry version (skip again only IF gate still fires) is strictly better: same upside in persistent regimes, no downside in regime-change moments. (d) Intersected secondary gate (criticizer's third suggestion): rejected because it strictly RESTRICTS skips, which is the wrong direction per the same evidence â€” AFG's existing skips are positive-precision, more should help. (e) Cap M=5 or M=10 instead of 3: chosen M=3 to balance regime capture against true-cascade risk; the hard cap is a safety net, not the primary mechanism.
proposer.revision_notes: Round 1 objections addressed: (A) MAJOR 'mis-identifies source of AFG edge â€” adaptive threshold relaxes the gate' â€” pivoted entirely; new proposal STRICTLY EXTENDS AFG's skip set rather than relaxing it. (B) MAJOR 'r1 failure shows skipping less is worse' â€” directly inverted: this proposal skips MORE (each successful AFG skip is now an opportunity for up to 3 chained skips during persistent regimes). (C) MAJOR 'unconsidered alternatives: tighten threshold or sticky cool-down' â€” adopted the sticky cool-down direction in a refined form (conditional re-entry rather than unconditional N-signal cool-down, eliminating the round-1 criticizer's concern about firing during regime reversals). The threshold-lowering alternative is acknowledged but deferred as a parallel direction. (D) MINOR 'imbalance_ratio=0.20 unmotivated' â€” moot; no ratio parameter in this proposal. (E) MINOR 'dimensional issue with total_volume' â€” moot.

objections.text: The hard cap max_consecutive_skips=3 may produce a FAILURE MODE worse than base AFG. Base AFG's anti-cascade _position_flat=True reset exists precisely because in a persistent adverse regime, the strategy continues firing signals into a losing direction; the unconditional re-entry is a deliberate floor on adverse-selection accumulation. By extending gating up to 3 successive signals, this proposal allows the strategy's open intent to accumulate over 3 seconds during persistent adverse flow â€” the regime is the same direction the strategy wants to enter, so when the cap finally fires, the strategy enters at a potentially worse price than if it had taken the entry 3s earlier (during the still-adverse but less-degraded regime). The hypothesis assumes the regime CLEARS before the cap, but if it persists beyond 3s, the deferred entry is into a deeper adverse hole. The proposer does not quantify or bound this downside.

Empirical interaction with the strategy not addressed. The proposer claims 'persistent regimes ~1-3s' but this is asserted without evidence. The strategy generates signals at 1.0s cadence; if a persistent adverse regime is also driving the SIGNAL (e.g., the oracle correctly fires SELL during sustained sell pressure), then chained skips would suppress entries that â€” over the oracle's 30s horizon â€” are actually correctly directional. Base AFG's reset is a way of saying 'after one skip, trust the signal.' Suppressing 3 consecutive skips might systematically destroy the strategy's directional conviction in exactly the regimes where it's strongest. Without empirical evidence on the joint distribution of (signal-direction, persistent-adverse-flow-direction), this is a real risk.
The cap of 3 is arbitrary â€” 'chosen to balance.' Why not 2 or 5? No empirical anchor. Acceptable as a first-attempt default with the falsifiable prediction, but acknowledge as parameter risk.

Implementation detail: in the conditional re-entry path (b), 'else skip again' increments consecutive_skips but does not set any post-skip state. The gate is re-evaluated naturally on the next order. This is correct but the state-machine should be made explicit in the implementation notes to avoid ambiguity.

suggested_alternatives: Add a directional condition to the chained-skip: only chain a skip if the new signal is in the SAME direction as the most recent skipped signal â€” protects against suppressing legitimate reversal signals.
criticizer.reasoning: The proposal correctly addresses round 1's directional error (now extends skips rather than relaxing them). However the chained-skip mechanism has a real downside path â€” extending gating into a persistent adverse regime that the strategy wants to ENTER directionally with may suppress the strategy's strongest signals; and the deferred-entry-into-worse-price risk for hard-cap scenarios is unbounded. A directional condition (only chain skips when the new signal is in the SAME direction as the skipped one) eliminates the suppress-legitimate-reversal failure mode at zero implementation cost.

proposer.mechanism: Persistent-Flow AFG (with directional-chain condition): identical to base AFG (single 10s rolling window of signed aggressor flow; skip BUY when net_flow<=-2.0, skip SELL when net_flow>=+2.0; reduce-only always submits; trade-tick subscription; look-ahead-free pruning), EXCEPT the post-skip anti-cascade is replaced with a directional conditional re-entry. State variables: consecutive_skips (int, default 0) and last_skipped_side (OrderSide or None, default None). After a skip, do NOT set _position_flat=True; instead increment consecutive_skips and set last_skipped_side=order.side. On the next open order with side S: (i) if consecutive_skips==0 (first signal or post-reset), apply AFG's normal gate â€” skip on adverse and update state, else submit and ensure state reset; (ii) if consecutive_skips>=1: if S != last_skipped_side (DIRECTION CHANGE â€” possible legitimate reversal), force-submit unconditionally and reset state (consecutive_skips=0, last_skipped_side=None); else if consecutive_skips>=max_consecutive_skips (default 3, hard cap), force-submit unconditionally and reset state; else evaluate AFG's gate â€” if it fires (still adverse in the same direction), skip and increment; if it does NOT fire (regime has cleared), submit and reset state. Default max_consecutive_skips=3.
proposer.inefficiency_exploited: Same as round 2: AFG's hard _position_flat=True reset wastes the gate's information on the very next signal after a skip, which (in a persistent adverse-flow regime) is highly likely to face the same adverse selection AFG just correctly identified. Persistent-Flow AFG extends gating across same-direction signals during the regime â€” but DOES NOT suppress signals in the reversed direction (which may be legitimate exit-and-flip moves). The directional condition addresses round 2's MAJOR objection: a reversal signal (e.g., previous SELL skipped, new signal BUY) suggests the regime is structurally different and should not be chain-suppressed. Combined with the hard cap, this gives bounded downside: at most 3 same-direction signals can be chained, and a direction-change always breaks the chain immediately.
proposer.why_survives_costs: Zero commission, zero slippage cost model (verified). Edge accrues entirely as realized_pnl. Base AFG: realized_pnl=$1255.50, +704.8% vs simple, skip rate 21.6%. Persistent-Flow AFG (with directional-chain) is expected to skip MORE than AFG on persistent-regime days, with the additional skips being structurally homogeneous (same direction, same adverse-flow regime) and therefore precision-positive. The directional condition ensures any legitimate reversal signal immediately breaks the chain â€” so the algo never suppresses a reversal entry, preserving full directional reactivity. Pre-committed falsifiable prediction: realized_pnl on the 12-day train window will exceed base AFG's $1255.50 by at least 5% (PASS margin). Failure modes: (a) if persistent regimes are rare in the train window (1-3s adverse regimes are not typical), the chained-skip path rarely fires and the algo behaves like AFG â€” flat outcome; (b) if persistent regimes commonly RESOLVE within the 3s cap such that the strategy's deferred entry is into a worse price than AFG's immediate entry, realized_pnl is worse than AFG â€” hypothesis falsified.
proposer.builds_on: aggressor-flow-gate (base) â€” preserves the signed-flow primitive, 10s window, 2.0 threshold, level-based skip criterion, reduce-only short-circuit, trade-tick subscription, look-ahead-free pruning. Replaces only the post-skip _position_flat=True reset with the directional-chain state machine described above. ALSO informed by afg-pc-r1 (negative result: skipping less than AFG underperforms by ~$767) and round 2 criticism (chained skips without direction check could suppress legitimate reversals).
proposer.alternatives_considered: Same set as round 2, plus: (g) chain only via flow-magnitude persistence (e.g., chain only if |net_flow| has GROWN since the prior skip) â€” rejected: adds parameter complexity (growth threshold) without clearly stronger discrimination than the simple direction check. (h) Probabilistic re-entry post-skip â€” rejected: introduces RNG, breaks determinism. (i) Longer hard cap (max=5) â€” defaulted to 3; if successful, cap is a parameter to sweep in follow-up runs.
proposer.revision_notes: Round 2 objections addressed: (A) MAJOR 'deferred-entry-into-worse-price unbounded' â€” bounded by the hard cap of 3 signals (~3s); same-direction chained skips and the cap are both explicitly bounded. Additionally, falsifiable prediction now explicitly enumerates the deferred-entry failure mode as a test of the hypothesis. (B) MAJOR 'suppresses legitimate directional reversal signals' â€” DIRECTLY FIXED by the directional condition: any order whose side differs from last_skipped_side immediately force-submits and resets state. Round 2 criticizer suggested this fix; adopted verbatim. (C) MINOR 'cap=3 arbitrary' â€” acknowledged; 3 chosen as balance between regime capture and deferred-entry risk; falsifiable prediction stands. (D) MINOR 'state machine ambiguity' â€” addressed by explicit enumeration of all branches in the mechanism description: (i) consecutive_skips==0; (ii.a) direction change; (ii.b) hard cap; (ii.c) gate not adverse; (ii.d) gate still adverse.

objections.text: Hard cap max_consecutive_skips=3 remains a parameter-tuning risk; acknowledged by proposer as secondary debug target with falsifiable prediction. Acceptable for first attempt.
Empirical overlap between extended skip set and base AFG's skip set is unknown until tested. The falsifiable >=5% realized_pnl improvement is a clean test. Acceptable inherent first-attempt risk.

criticizer.reasoning: Mechanism is logically coherent, strictly extends base AFG's skip set (addressing round 1's directional error), has the directional-condition guard that addresses round 2's reversal-suppression objection, has an explicit bounded hard cap addressing the deferred-entry risk, and commits to a falsifiable >=5% improvement prediction. No remaining BLOCKING or MAJOR objections; no clearly superior untried alternative within the AFG-refinement family that wasn't already considered.
